# E02: paired leave-one-out ablation

E02 compares the reversible, opt-in Phase-4 type-aware eviction component
(`treatment-type-aware`) with the immediately preceding Phase-4 FIFO policy
(`baseline-fifo`). The comparison is a paired leave-one-out ablation. Both
conditions run against an injected production `RuntimeMemoryStore`; no mock
provider, network access, or product configuration change is permitted.

## Pre-registration

The fixture is committed before execution in
`shared/agent-dev/paired-ablation-fixture.json`. The primary metric is
`pass^3`: the proportion of fixture cases for which all three paired
repetitions succeed. Secondary metrics are ordinary success rate, latency p50
and p95, token proxy, false-block count/rate, and safety-violation
count/rate. The fixture fixes 24 cases, three repetitions, paired seeds, and a
2000-resample paired bootstrap. Latency and token budgets and permitted increases
in false blocks and safety violations are also fixed in the fixture.

The runner must reject fixtures with fewer than 20 cases, unequal repetition
counts, duplicate case IDs, or non-finite measurements. It must validate that
at least one retained/evicted set differs between conditions before reporting
an effect.

## Execution contract

1. Construct isolated stores for each condition and case.
2. Insert fixture inputs in the fixed case order and use the same paired seed
   for baseline and treatment.
3. Record success, latency, token proxy, false block, safety violation, and
   retained/evicted memory identifiers.
4. Compute condition summaries and paired treatment-minus-baseline effects.
5. Compute two-sided 95% percentile bootstrap intervals from paired case
   deltas using a deterministic local PRNG.
6. Report zero and negative effects without reinterpretation or selection of a
   winner.
7. Check all pre-registered degradation budgets and label any failure.

The implementation does not spawn processes, call providers, mutate product
defaults, alter product locks, or alter approval policy. The runtime adapter is
responsible for creating a fresh, isolated real store for every case and for
selecting the requested Phase-4 policy.

## Acceptance evidence

A completed run must include the activation check, both condition summaries,
all paired effects and confidence intervals, budget evaluation, and the
internal-only disclosure. Results remain an internal evaluation artifact even
when the treatment is beneficial.

# Paired ablation boundary

This rule applies to `scripts/lib/paired-ablation.mjs` and every E02 report.

## Required

- The only conditions are Phase-4 FIFO baseline and Phase-4 type-aware
  treatment.
- The runtime adapter must use the production `RuntimeMemoryStore` and a fresh
  isolated store for each case.
- Use only the committed deterministic local fixture. Do not call a provider or
  use live credentials.
- Preserve case order, paired seeds, the pre-registered primary metric,
  repetition count, bootstrap configuration, and degradation budgets.
- Verify component activation by finding at least one difference in retained or
  evicted identifiers.
- Publish success, `pass^k`, p50/p95 latency, token proxy, false blocks, safety
  violations, treatment-minus-baseline effects, and two-sided 95% intervals.
- Report negative and zero effects faithfully.

## Forbidden

- Changing product defaults, product locks, approval behavior, dependencies, or
  permissions.
- Selecting conditions or seeds after observing results.
- Filtering failures, replacing the fixture, or presenting a favorable metric as
  the primary result.
- Claiming that a component is active without retained/evicted evidence.
- Adding network, provider, subprocess, credential, or test-reading behavior.
- Presenting an internal evaluation as a user-visible product change.

The four README languages are intentionally unchanged because this package has
no user-visible behavior or documentation change.

# E02 paired ablation closure

## Scope

E02 is an internal, opt-in evaluation of one reversible component: Phase-4
type-aware eviction. Its paired leave-one-out baseline is the immediately
preceding Phase-4 FIFO policy. Results are produced with the production
`RuntimeMemoryStore`; the deterministic local fixture contains no provider
credentials and performs no network access.

## Metrics and method

The fixture pre-registers 24 cases, three repetitions, paired seeds, and the
primary `pass^3` metric: a case contributes to `pass^3` only when every one of
its three repetitions succeeds. Reports also include ordinary success rate,
latency p50/p95, mean and p95 token proxy, false-block count/rate, safety
violation count/rate, and paired treatment-minus-baseline effects with
two-sided 95% percentile-bootstrap intervals.

Baseline and treatment use isolated stores, identical insertion order, and the
same seed for each paired case/repetition. Before calculating effects, the
runner requires retained/evicted evidence that the type-aware component was
active in at least one case.

## Reading a result

The direction of every effect is treatment minus baseline. Positive success or
`pass^k` effects favor type-aware eviction; positive latency and token-proxy
effects are degradations. Negative and zero values are valid findings and must
not be hidden, relabeled, or explained away by selecting another metric.
Confidence intervals quantify fixture uncertainty only; they do not establish
general product benefit.

Budget failures are reported explicitly. A favorable result is still limited to
internal evaluation and does not change the product default, product lock,
approval behavior, or any user-visible contract. The four README translations
remain unchanged because this work adds no user-visible behavior.

## Reproducibility

Use `shared/agent-dev/paired-ablation-fixture.json` without editing it after a
run. Record the fixture version, activation evidence, condition summaries,
paired effects, confidence intervals, and budget evaluation together. The
implementation is side-effect free: it does not invoke providers, spawn
processes, read tests, or access credentials.
